sections.html:
The county treasurer is the main office. It takes in and passes along current and delinquent real estate tax, keeps the primary tax records, and also handles tax foreclosure sales, unclaimed funds and lottery tax credits. Stop by 1516 Church Street, Stevens Point, WI 54481 (weekdays 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.) or phone (715) 346-1348.

Some bills bypass the county. On the first installment the treasurer collects for 23 of 28 municipalities, and on the second for 27 of 28. Stevens Point owners pay the city their current taxes, while a few towns and a village keep the first installment local. Your bill's coupons name the payee.

sections.h2: Due dates and where to pay
sections.html:
The county bills once a year, with two stubs for January 31 and July 31 and no reminder notices. That matches the Wis. Stat. 74.11 default. Under the same statute, a parcel whose tax totals less than $100 is paid in one sum by January 31.

Where the parcel isWho gets the paymentInstallments
City of Stevens PointCity of Stevens Point treasurerThree: January 31, April 30, July 31
Towns of Almond, Belmont, Lanark and Village of MilladoreThe municipal treasurer for the first installmentCounty takes the second
Towns of Alban, Amherst, Buena Vista, Carson, Dewey, Grant, Hull, Linwood, New Hope, Pine Grove, Plover, Sharon, StocktonPortage County TreasurerAll installments
Villages of Almond, Amherst, Amherst Junction, Junction City, Nelsonville, Park Ridge, Plover, Rosholt, WhitingPortage County TreasurerAll installments

The county also collects delinquent City of Stevens Point taxes.

Choices include mail, the office window, a partner bank, the website and the phone. Checks and cash cost nothing at the window or by mail. Online payment lives at landinfo.co.portage.wi.gov, operated by Point and Pay, which bills its fees to the taxpayer.

  • Credit cards run 2.39 percent of the payment, whether online or by phone.
  • A Visa debit card costs $3.95 online or 2.39 percent by phone, and other debit cards are treated like credit.
  • An electronic check is $1.50.
  • The automated phone line, 1-877-782-4828, prompts for your tax year and bill number.
  • Three banks take payments: Community First Bank in Rosholt, International Bank of Amherst and Pineries Bank in Stevens Point.

For an online parcel search, type the parcel number alone, exactly as formatted on the bill. Mail goes to Portage County Treasurer at the Church Street address.

Five working days of grace pass, and on the sixth business day the tax is delinquent. A missed date also ends the second-installment option and makes the full bill due. The county charges 1.5 percent a month on the unpaid balance beginning the month after the due date: 1.5 percent shows up right after the grace period and 3 percent by March. Additional fees can apply, so ask for a final payoff.

At the state level, Wis. Stat. 74.47 sets the floor at one percent per month or part of one, and a county board may add up to 0.5 percent monthly by ordinance.

  • Still unpaid on September 1? A tax certificate is issued and the owner receives a Notice of Issuance of Tax Certificate.
  • From there the owner has two years to clear that year's balance.
  • If two years pass without payment, the county takes the property through the tax deed process.
  • No payment plans exist for delinquent taxes, yet any amount is accepted whenever you can pay it.

Help may exist: the Foundation for Rural Housing, acting through the State of Wisconsin, funds several situations including delinquent taxes. Its numbers are 608-238-3448 and 888-400-5974.

sections.h2: Paying the City of Stevens Point
sections.html:
Current taxes in the city are paid in three parts at the city's own treasurer, 1515 Strongs Avenue, weekdays 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The three bottom coupons fall on January 31, April 30 and July 31. A single missed payment makes all that is unpaid delinquent, with one percent monthly interest running from February 1, and the county layers on penalties if the tax is still delinquent after July 31.

Look up bills, due dates and a future-dated payoff on the city's website. Fees there: $1.50 per e-check, 1.5 percent on debit and 2.40 percent on credit, each card type with a $2.00 minimum. Delinquent taxes from earlier years belong to the county treasurer, 715-346-1348. Spot a star under the parcel number on your bill? That marks a prior year delinquency.

Three credits show up on a Portage County bill:

  • School levy tax credit: automatic, on every bill.
  • First dollar credit: automatic, for a parcel that has an improvement.
  • Lottery and gaming credit: for your primary residence, and you must ask for it, for a single parcel.

Eligibility means owning a dwelling in Wisconsin and living there as your primary home on January 1. Rental units, business property, vacant land and garages are left out. Apply through the treasurer by the January 31 after your bill comes, or make a late claim to the Department of Revenue by October 1. Mill rate sheets for 2021 through 2025 are posted by the treasurer.

Both the assessor and the board of review sit at the municipal level, so begin with the clerk of the city, town or village where the house is. The clerk gives you the assessor's details and the review dates. Under Wis. Stat. 70.47 the board clerk needs your notice of intent 48 hours before the board first meets, and your written objection is due in that meeting's first two hours, unless good cause waives the notice.

Assessors are listed by town, village and city, so the municipal clerk is the right first call.

Identify the office that holds your bill and request its payoff figure before you pick a closing date. In Stevens Point you deal with the city on current taxes and the county on delinquent ones. In most other places the second installment sits with the county treasurer.

  • A finished electronic real estate transfer return must accompany any conveyance of an ownership interest; you prepare it on the Department of Revenue website.
  • Sign up for Property Fraud Alert, through the county's recorder, to be told of filings under your name.
  • The county's Tapestry site searches land records, and the Wisconsin Real Estate Sales Finder lists sales.
  • Your contract decides how the year's tax splits between buyer and seller, so check with the closing agent.

If back taxes are unpaid, a cash buyer can usually close fast and have the payoff taken from your proceeds at closing, which avoids the 1.5 percent monthly interest running longer.

An estimated 71,943 people lived here on July 1, 2025, a 2.2 percent gain since 2020. Of homes, 69.7 percent are owner-occupied with a median value of $243,100; median gross rent is $940. Households total 29,679 and housing units 32,398. Permits issued in 2025 numbered 244.

faqs.a: The county's two installments land on January 31 and July 31. Stevens Point runs three, on January 31, April 30 and July 31. Reminders aren't mailed, so note the dates yourself.

To the county treasurer on Church Street, with exceptions: the City of Stevens Point, the Towns of Almond, Belmont and Lanark, and the Village of Milladore. The towns and village use their own treasurer for the first installment, and the city for every current one.
1.5 percent monthly on the unpaid balance, from the month after the due date. State law supplies one percent, with up to 0.5 percent more at county option. Phone (715) 346-1348 for a payoff.
Unpaid on September 1 triggers a tax certificate and starts a two-year window to pay. If it isn't paid by then, the county forecloses by tax deed.

faqs.q: Can I set up a payment plan?
faqs.a: No formal plans exist for late taxes, but partial payments are welcome any time. The Foundation for Rural Housing, 608-238-3448, has funds for some delinquent situations.
